about: On Augustine of Canterbury’s feast, the community offers sacrifice and humbly asks that the sheep who were lost may be nourished by this saving food after their return to the one fold.

s01.translation: Lord, we offer sacrifice to You on the feast of blessed Augustine, Your bishop and confessor, humbly praying that the sheep who were lost, once they have returned to the one fold, may be nourished by this saving food. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God,

alignments.gloss: having returned to the one fold

w006.explanation: Solemnitas is the feast of Augustine being celebrated by the offering community. It is not an act of celebration performed by Augustine himself.

w008.explanation: This May 28 prayer honors Augustine of Canterbury, whose feast is the occasion of the offering. He is not Monica’s son Augustine of Hippo.

w014.explanation: The same community both offers and humbly entreats. Deprecantes has active meaning, although its dictionary verb is deponent.

w018.explanation: Being lost belongs to the sheep-and-fold image. The prayer does not describe literal death followed by bodily resurrection.

w022.explanation: The sheep themselves return. Their return precedes the nourishment being requested, but the participle does not independently say that the return was completed before this prayer is spoken.

w025.explanation: The saving food continues the sheep-and-fold image in a prayer over the sacrifice. The demonstrative hoc points to this nourishment, not an unrelated future meal.
